args: In mruby/src/gc.c, analyze mrb_realloc_simple() and mrb_realloc() around lines 207-237, especially the explicit mrb_free(mrb, p) when allocation fails. What ownership semantics does mruby require from allocf/realloc, and are there any callers that intentionally rely on mrb_realloc freeing the old pointer before mrb_raise_nomemory? Would removing only that mrb_free call preserve expected behavior, including custom allocators and len == 0 behavior? Also identify any relevant allocation API documentation or tests.

The provided ASan report shows a double-free after ary_expand_capa in mruby/src/array.c calls mrb_realloc on an existing array buffer for a multi-exabyte request. mrb_realloc_simple returns NULL while retaining the old allocation under realloc semantics; mrb_realloc then explicitly frees that old pointer and raises. Because the assignment in ary_expand_capa never completes after the nonlocal exception, the RArray retains the pointer and obj_free frees it during mrb_close. I have inspected mruby/src/gc.c lines 207-237: mrb_realloc_simple invokes allocf, optionally runs full GC and retries; mrb_realloc returns directly for len zero, but on NULL for positive len it currently frees p, sets out_of_memory, and raises. I suspect the root fix is simply to remove mrb_free(mrb, p), but want to verify project allocator contracts and whether another subtle state update is required.
